Dashboard: CODARIS Web Frameworks & Technologies Research Dataset

IMPORTANT: React is a library, Node.js/Deno/Bun are runtimes, WordPress/Drupal are CMS platforms, and CSS systems such as Tailwind/Bootstrap are styling frameworks. CODARIS should keep these types separate. The shared catalogue exists for discovery, not to claim every entry is the same kind of technology.

POPULARITY: Stack Overflow percentages describe survey respondents who reported extensive use in the prior year. State of JS percentages describe its JavaScript-community respondents. W3Techs measures detected technologies on websites. These metrics are not directly interchangeable and should never be averaged into a single universal usage percentage.

Methodology: Issue
CODARIS treatment
Reason
Framework vs library vs runtime
Keep an explicit Type field. React is a library; Node.js/Deno/Bun are runtimes; WordPress/Drupal are CMS platforms.
Developer surveys often group heterogeneous web technologies together, but educational pages should not erase technical distinctions.
Catalogue scope
Broad curated catalogue of 631 technologies gathered across major ecosystem comparison/awesome lists.
There is no authoritative finite list of every web framework ever created. This is a researched educational catalogue, not a claim of total completeness.
Stack Overflow usage
Use the 2025 'Have Used' percentage only for entries measured in that survey.
23,678 respondents answered the web-framework/technology question; it is multi-select and self-selected.
State of JS
Keep its usage/satisfaction values separate from Stack Overflow.
State of JS samples the JavaScript community and uses different questions/denominators.
Website market share
Use W3Techs only as detected website technology share and label the snapshot date.
Website deployment share is not the same as developer usage, npm downloads, jobs, or framework satisfaction.
Country breakdown
Do not infer framework usage from the overall country distribution.
A respondent being in a country does not tell us which framework they use; cross-tabs need direct source data.
Gender breakdown
Leave per-framework gender data blank unless a survey explicitly supports the cross-tab with sample sizes and all response categories.
Inventing male/female percentages would create false demographic precision and discard non-binary/non-response categories.
Ranking
Rank only within a named source and metric, such as Stack Overflow 2025 usage.
A universal framework rank would mix incomparable measurements and silently encode editorial preferences.
Historical projects
Retain some legacy frameworks when they are relevant to web history or existing production estates.
Educational coverage should explain both modern and legacy stacks without implying equal current adoption.
